entries.claim: The stale-spine replay was written in plan 5 (04f2bcd), before plan 6 added the conflict check (df590a3), and it was never updated. Its recorded `/seldon prd` turn applies a PRD change over a spine with a conflicting decision with no conflict report, no conflict question and no go-ahead. At HEAD, SKILL.md ("The PRD rerun" and "The conflict check", lines 830-881) forbids that for this exact file state, so the replay that serves as Phase 7 success criterion 2's evidence for 'the next /seldon after an applied PRD change' depicts a transcript the shipped skill cannot produce.
entries.failure_scenario: I ran the stale-spine seed and the prd-conflict seed. The PRD-turn state the stale-spine history implies (spine-rerun/brief.md, which is byte-identical to prd-rerun/brief.md, sha256 38cbca64db3f39c8, plus samples/prd.md and samples/spine.md) is exactly the prd-conflict seed. On that state HEAD must name S-03, which quotes "a reminder when something's due" just as LOAN-03 does, then end on "Do you want me to apply this change to the PRD anyway?" with nothing edited, and evals/prd-conflict asserts exactly that. Yet stale-spine's history line 2 shows `/seldon prd` going straight to "I brought .planning/seldon/prd.md in line with the brief... LOAN-03... is retired" and the PRD confirm question. HEAD reaches an applied, conflicting PRD change only through the conflict question and a go-ahead (prd-conflict-apply). No case replays that go-ahead and then runs the next bare /seldon into the spine rerun. prd-conflict-apply stops at the PRD confirm. So the go-ahead-then-spine-rerun path is untested end to end, and the eval cited for criterion 2 rests on a history that contradicts the skill under test. The stale-spine graders still pass, because the /clear words make its test turn a new run that reads only the files, which is why per-plan review missed this.
